note: Receiver cases. Each gives the perigraph attributes of one record and what a conforming receiver does with them: `rejected` (not a record of this version), or `stored` with whether a verdict over this record alone is `admitted` or `refused` (SPEC section 0.5). A rejected case says whether spec/schema/record.schema.json alone rejects it too (`schema`): the ones it accepts are rejected only by recomputing an identity. Run them with tools/conform.py. Comparisons between records are not covered here; see conformance/README.md.

cases.description: A record from a request adapter: instruction held, the rest absent, the model half not_observable.
The same record with a model half a stamper loaded, carrying model and artifact identities.
No model half at all. It does not conform as a sender's record, and a receiver still stores it and does not refuse a verdict for it.
Most parts are not mentioned at all. A record missing any number of parts is stored, never rejected; the parts must_be_known_for_identity names are held or not_provided, so it keeps its identity.
A manifest naming a part twice is read as a set.
Empty entries in a manifest are dropped, not read as a part named empty-string.
A vendor extension key is ignored, never grounds for rejection.
Attributes outside the perigraph. prefix belong to the span and are not the record's.
Status collector_failed: stored as a log, and no verdict.
Status aborted: stored as a log, and no verdict.
No identifying part, so no harness identity: stored, no verdict.
The manifest claims tool_schemas and the record reports it not_reachable.

cases.description: The harness identity attribute is omitted while the parts derive one: the receiver reads the derived value.
An instruction and a request template, both held: the identity is over both.
A request template held with no instruction: refines_only, so the record has no harness identity.
A record states an identity over a request template alone, which refines_only forbids: the stated identity is not the derived one.
A record whose request template is extraction_failed states the instruction-only identity: read_for_identity withdraws it, so the stated identity is not the derived one.
An instruction held and a request template that did not verify: no harness identity, so no verdict.
An instruction held and the request template neither held nor absent: it might have been there, so read_for_identity withdraws the identity. The record is stored, and no verdict is given.
A held request template and the instruction-only identity stated: the derived identity covers both parts, so the stated one is not it.
An instruction held and the request template withheld as redacted: must_be_known_for_identity withdraws the identity.
A request template held and the instruction extraction_failed: the template refines only, and the instruction is not known, so there is no identity.

attributes.perigraph.absent.instruction.detail: messages[0].content is an array, not a string

cases.description: A request template declared by its owner beside a held instruction. From version 4 a declaration does not stand in for a part must_be_known_for_identity names: only a template held in the request, or absent as not_provided, lets the instruction's identity stand, so the record has no identity and is refused.
An instruction and generation controls held in the request at canonical_value: the identity is over both.
Unlisted request members named, and two counted: stored and admitted; the names never key.
perigraph.request.unlisted without perigraph.request.unlisted_omitted.
perigraph.request.unlisted_omitted without perigraph.request.unlisted.
A negative unlisted count.
An unlisted entry outside the binding's name pattern.
An unlisted entry the binding reads: the part read from it is incomplete.
More unlisted names than unlisted_names_max.
A stated identity computed over the instruction alone, when generation_controls is held: not the identity the parts derive.
Generation controls held and no instruction: they name no prompt text, so they establish no identity (refines_only).
Generation controls declared by the owner beside a held instruction: a declaration does not stand in for a part must_be_known_for_identity names, so there is no identity.
Generation controls held in the request at parsed: not the boundary keying_boundary lists, so they key nothing and the identity is withdrawn.
Generation controls the collector could not serialise: no identity.
